sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who are the users, what is the job, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: Derives turns per second at average and peak from 3M conversations and the 4x factor
Quantifies the largest tenant's flash-sale load
Names per-tier SLOs and a cost or margin target
Lists what is out of scope

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the platform as layers: what runs in each, what it hands to the next, and why it exists.
criteria: Includes admission control, a config service, a durable workflow engine and an event log as layers
Shows where tenant identity is set and that every layer below enforces it
States one idea about where tenant isolation lives

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: What data does each tenant bring, how does it reach the model, and how do syncs stay fair?
criteria: Separates indexed knowledge from live systems reached by tools
Stores tenant credentials per tenant in a secrets manager
Schedules ingestion per tenant so one large import cannot starve others

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How do 10M chunks get built and kept fresh for 200 tenants?
criteria: States chunking, metadata including tenant id, and an embedding model
Sizes the index in GB or the re-embed cost in dollars
Re-processes only changed content
Avoids isolation by metadata filter alone, or explains why it is safe

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: How does one agent graph serve 200 different configurations?
criteria: Pins a config version for the length of a conversation
Routes turns between a small and a mid model with a stated split
Hands long-running actions to a durable workflow rather than running them in the chat turn
Keeps step limits and model choice as validated config, not prompt text

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What is remembered per thread, user and tenant, and how is it kept separate?
criteria: Keys memory by tenant and user and enforces it with RLS or equivalent
Uses per-tenant encryption keys and explains offboarding or deletion
Rules out sharing learned memory across tenants

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: How are per-tenant tools, credentials and limits handled?
criteria: Resolves tenant credentials inside the tool gateway, never in the orchestrator or prompt
Computes effective permission as an intersection of tenant, user and agent scopes
Enforces a platform-wide money ceiling in code above any tenant setting
Uses idempotency keys on writes

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What are the runtime and admin APIs, and how is the latency budget spent?
criteria: Splits time to first token by stage and the total fits the Enterprise SLO
Has admin endpoints that create, evaluate and promote config versions
Signs outbound webhooks
Explains how tiers get different latency under load

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What does the platform cost per month and per tier, and which lever moves it most?
criteria: Shows monthly cost with and without routing and prompt caching
Breaks cost down per tier with cache hit rates
Orders the prompt so a shared prefix is reused across tenants
Keys every cache by tenant

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Which stores hold what, how big are they, and how does the layout enforce isolation?
criteria: Sizes each store
Partitions vectors per tenant or gives a tested alternative
Feeds an event log into an analytics store for metering
Justifies the vector store choice with a measured number

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does the platform return, and what does every turn emit for metering?
criteria: Defines typed events including action status from the workflow
Emits a usage event per turn with tokens, cached tokens and model
Renders receipts from workflow results, not model text

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: What enforces isolation, money limits and fair capacity if a prompt or tenant pushes on them?
criteria: Proves isolation continuously, for example with planted canary documents
Defines admission thresholds that degrade, queue and shed by tier
Caps a surging tenant with a number and says what its overflow gets
Keeps money and permission limits in code

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: How do you know the platform is working for tenants and for the business?
criteria: Tracks resolution per tenant, not only the platform average
Attributes cost per tenant including cached-token discounts
States margin or revenue against model spend
Sends quota alerts at fixed thresholds

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks on a shared platform, and how is the blast radius limited?
criteria: Covers a noisy-neighbor surge
Covers provider rate limits or outage with failover
Covers a bad tenant config with eval gate, canary and rollback
Covers a crash mid-action without duplicate execution

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it, and what number unlocks each step?
criteria: Builds isolation and its tests before agent features
Ends each step with a measurable number
Onboards tenants in cohorts rather than all at once
